findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch_html, browse_page, fetch_parsed, list_elements, fetch_markdown, search_and_read, run_plugin, amazon_search, amazon_product, amazon_reviews, walmart_search, ebay_search, google_shopping, google_local, maps_place_details, google_images, youtube_search, youtube_transcript, zillow_search, indeed_jobs, trustpilot_reviews, booking_hotels · Private data: google_images, trustpilot_reviews · Public sink: browse_page, amazon_search · Destructive: browse_page, google_search, run_plugin.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch_html, browse_page, fetch_parsed, list_elements, fetch_markdown, search_and_read, run_plugin, amazon_search, amazon_product, amazon_reviews, walmart_search, ebay_search, google_shopping, google_local, maps_place_details, google_images, youtube_search, youtube_transcript, zillow_search, indeed_jobs, trustpilot_reviews, booking_hotels · Private data: google_images, trustpilot_reviews · Public sink: browse_page, amazon_search · Destructive: browse_page, google_search, run_plugin

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "fetch_html" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
